rows.description: A raised voice and hard face make the child freeze or cry, and she cannot yet understand why. Best is a short, calm no with the reason in a few words, and a hug when she settles.

rows.description: Being called bad or naughty makes the child feel she is wrong, not that the act was wrong. Wise adults name the behaviour, not the child: we do not hit, you are still loved.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear
related mind states: affection, shame

rows.description: The toddler screams back, throws or hits after a scolding: overwhelmed, not disrespectful. Adults keep their tone steady, hold the limit, and help the child calm before teaching.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, shame
related mind states: admiration, anger, calm, overwhelm

rows.description: Clapping and smiling when the child stacks blocks or takes steps makes her glow and repeat the effort. Praise the effort and the action, warm and specific, not just appearance.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection
related mind states: pride

rows.description: A grandmother's cheerful blessing and hug after a small achievement makes the child feel special and safe. Enjoy it, and keep rules and routines consistent across adults.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: pride
related mind states: joy, affection, trust

rows.description: When a parent is often absent in mind, the child tries louder cries or clinging, and if that fails may withdraw. Caregivers can repair with short, regular, fully present moments every day.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger
related mind states: detachment, resentment

rows.description: The toddler tantrums, throws things or screams to get noticed: even angry attention beats none. Respond to the need calmly, praise calm asking, and avoid rewarding only the storm.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: neglect
related mind states: anger, calm

rows.description: A rocking hold, a soft voice and words like I am here teach the child that big feelings end and someone helps. Repeated often, this becomes the base of her own self-calming.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence
related mind states: calm, trust

rows.description: The child seeks the lap, lullaby and smell of a familiar elder when hurt or sleepy. This is healthy attachment. Elders should comfort freely; parents need not feel replaced.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: trust

rows.description: The toddler folds hands, rings the bell, claps or bows because the family does, drawn by sound, lamp and loved faces. It is imitation and belonging, not belief. Keep it warm and never forced.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, awe
